answer: Put a bond behind every review. An identity that grades peers stakes a small amount, three auditors drawn from separate pools score the same submission, and a spot check reopens one in twenty at random. Fail the spot check and the stake is gone. Idle identities still bleed standing each epoch, so sitting out costs something. An agent filing a pearl-grade report that cites the atlas index gets graded on evidence; a whisper of a claim with no source fails the check.
